en.askTitle: Change the boxes to your own situation and get the same Japan stay plan, budget and checklist
en.runTitle: Remote US tester planning six months in Tokyo and Fukuoka on the digital-nomad status

fields.label: Arrival, departure and other Japan visits
fields.value: About 6 months from April 2027, Tokyo first

fields.label: Employer, salary and written permission
fields.value: Fully remote QA tester for a US company, US$118,000 a year

fields.label: Insurance needs
fields.value: Private health insurance for the whole stay

en.template: Help me plan a Japan stay for {passport}, {trip}, {employer}, {housing} and {insurance}. Separate visa eligibility, employer/payroll approval and treaty questions. Build an itemized budget, housing shortlist and document checklist; flag what needs a consulate, insurer or tax professional to confirm. Ask before contacting anyone, applying, booking, buying cover or uploading personal documents.

phases.title: Read the official immigration, tax, insurance and housing pages
phases.note: Visa rules, tax treaty, insurance prices, eight dated listings
phases.judgment: It kept conflicting evidence in view instead of smoothing it over: one share house showed different prices and terms on its two sales channels, so both were recorded as found; a “zero deposit” ad was flagged because it left out separately listed initial charges; and no April 2027 availability was claimed.

phases.title: Build the guide with the eligibility checklist, budget table, timeline and every calculation shown
phases.judgment: It did not tell the user that six months means no Japanese tax. The tax treaty exemption needs all three conditions to be met at once, and 1 April to 30 September 2027 is 183 days counted inclusively, so one more day breaks the day-count test.

phases.title: Independent review of the arithmetic and of the page on desktop and phone widths
phases.judgment: The independent reviewer recomputed every currency conversion in the budget, the insurance examples and the day counts, and found no discrepancy. It also said plainly what it had not rechecked: the official immigration pages, and a full re-audit of all eight listings, which it only sampled.

workers: Found eight real housing listings in Tokyo and Fukuoka, furnished monthly flats and share houses, and wrote down prices, deposits and fees
Compared the published prices and benefits of two travel-health insurance plans and read the official tax rules for a US employee working in Japan
Re-read the finished guide and recomputed the budget conversions and day counts on its own
